data.title: CDC Says Cyclospora Outbreak Is Over
data.description:
By Kelly Cloonan

Public-health officials declared an end to a cyclosporiasis outbreak that spread across the U.S. this summer.

The outbreak, which federal health officials linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Mexican supplier Taylor Farms, has resulted in a total of 12,883 reported cases of the gastrointestinal food-borne illness across 21 states, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said Friday.

The CDC said the contaminated lettuce linked to the outbreak is no longer available in stores or restaurants, and the products' best-by dates have passed.

Additionally, recent infections linked to the outbreak have declined, with fewer than two infections per day on average in August compared to a peak of more than 1,000 daily infections, the CDC said.

The Food and Drug Administration said it continues to investigate how the product linked to the outbreak became contaminated with cyclospora, the parasite that causes cyclosporiasis.

Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com

data.description:

  • Freight rates including from West Africa have soared to record highs after the last escalation in the Middle East war, potentially impacting demand.

data.title: Artisan Partners Shares Fall on $6B Rebalancing From Modified Client Relationship
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Shares of Artisan Partners were down after the company said it expects to rebalance around $6 billion from its Global Value strategy this month as a result of a modified relationship with a client.

Shares were down 3.2% to $38.42 as of Friday afternoon. The stock has shed 5.7% so far this year.

The company said after the close Thursday that a long-standing, sub-advisory client is shifting to a multi-manager structure from a single-manager structure, with Artisan remaining as one of three managers.

The move will have a lesser impact on revenue than on assets under management, the company said, "given the nature of the mandate and its associated fee structure."

The company reported $183.5 billion in preliminary assets under management as of Aug. 31, with Artisan Funds and Artisan Global Funds making up $94.5 billion of that total.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Lawyer cites fake witnesses in murder case and blames ChatGPT
data.description:
Key points:
  • Lawyer's filing included invented witnesses and fabricated police testimony, court says
  • Attorney said he used ChatGPT and called the lapse an honest mistake
  • New Mexico justice said at hearing that AI hallucination risks are widely known among lawyers

By Mike Scarcella

A defense lawyer appealing his client's murder conviction submitted a brief containing made-up police testimony and witnesses fabricated by OpenAI's ChatGPT, New Mexico's highest court said.

The New Mexico Supreme Court on Wednesday fined the attorney, Stephen Aarons, and held him in contempt for failing to verify the accuracy of the court filing, which Aarons said he prepared with help from the AI program.

The filing “contained false testimony from wholly fabricated witnesses,” the court said.

The panel also said Aarons had “demonstrated a lack of remorse and a lack of concern for his client.” The justices fined Aarons $5,000 and said they will refer him to an attorney disciplinary board for investigation.

Aarons in a statement to Reuters said he had used ChatGPT to summarize the trial proceedings when he agreed to take up the defendant's appeal last year, and did not understand the degree to which AI could "hallucinate" facts.

"I am remorseful but hopeful that the disciplinary board takes into account it was an honest mistake," he said. "It is a lesson learned for all professionals who rely upon this powerful but sometimes unstable technology."

OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The court’s sanction is the latest in a growing number of cases in which state and federal judges have disciplined lawyers for submitting court documents generated by AI tools without adequately vetting them. Some judges have also faced scrutiny over the use of AI.

Dozens of lawyers have been sanctioned for filing briefs where AI made up case ​citations or misquoted the law. Aarons’ filing appears to have gone further, containing fabricated witness testimony in a criminal appeal.

Aarons, a private attorney based in Santa Fe, was handling the appeal of Oscar Renee Sandoval, who pleaded not guilty to the murder of the mother of his children before he was convicted and sentenced last year to life in prison.

The appeal is still pending and was assigned on September 2 to Kim Chavez Cook, a New Mexico public defender. Cook declined to comment.

The district attorney's office for Doña Ana County also declined to comment.

The state supreme court last month ordered Aarons to explain how the fabricated material, which it said appeared to include "fictional statements that the shooter was wearing dark pants and a white shirt," was included in his primary brief in the appeal.

Aarons told the court at an August 21 hearing that he fed a computer-generated transcript and other case materials to ChatGPT, presuming it would generate "a bulletproof summary."

The justices sounded incredulous that Aarons was not fully aware of how AI can make mistakes.

"Counsel, do you watch the news? Do you listen to the radio? Do you read anything about what's going on in the world?" Justice C. Shannon Bacon said at the hearing. "Because the problem with lawyers relying on AI hallucinations is an above-the-fold story every single day.”

data.title: Spider-Man’s box-office reign could get tangled up by ‘Practical Magic 2’
data.description:
Warner Bros. Discovery is looking to take the top spot at the North American box office this weekend with “Practical Magic 2,” as the Warner Bros. sequel opens against Sony Group’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which has led the domestic chart for six consecutive weekends.

Forecasts for the Sandra Bullock-Nicole Kidman sequel vary. Boxoffice Pro projects a $40 million-$50 million opening, while Variety expects $30 million-$40 million from about 4,000 North American theaters. The trade publication expects “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” to take in $9 million to $11 million in its seventh weekend, while Universal’s "The Odyssey" is projected at $6 million to $8 million.

The “Practical Magic” sequel is being released by Warner Bros. at a time when the major-studio release calendar has been relatively light, giving the film a chance to capture demand after a record-setting summer for US theaters. Boxoffice Pro described it as the week’s destination movie by default amid the shortage of major studio releases.

For “Spider-Man,” the weekend could mark another milestone even as it loses the top spot. The Sony-Marvel film is closing in on the domestic box-office record held by “Star Wars: The Force Awakens,” which finished its run with about $936.7 million. Current tracking expects “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” to surpass that mark this weekend, ending the more than decade-long reign of “The Force Awakens.”

The weekend follows a record US summer box office of about $4.76 billion, underscoring the strong momentum heading into the fall release slate.

data.title: Grain Trader Focus Expected to Quickly Shift — Market Talk
data.description: The WASDE report showed some changes to U.S. corn and soybean production and yields, which sparked some selling of futures in afternoon trading. But the lasting impact of the WASDE isn't expected to linger long in the minds of grain traders, says the Hightower Report in a note. "Without a surprise in this report, the market will quickly return to trading other fundamentals such as South American weather and China demand, which has been very strong this week," says the firm in a note, in reference to soybean market conditions. Rallying in corn futures is also not expected to rally much on the report's data. CBOT corn is now down 0.5%, while soybeans fall 2.4% and wheat sheds 2.4%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

data.title: Pharming wins approval of Joenja for younger age group
data.description:
Key points:
  • The US FDA has approved Pharming Group's Joenja (leniolisib) for children between the ages of four and 11 with a kind of rare genetic immune system disorder.
  • The treatment was previously approved in 2023 for individuals 12 years and older with activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS).
  • Approval was based on safety and pharmacokinetic data from a single-arm, open-label study.
  • Individuals with APDS suffer from recurrent infections, especially in the sinuses, ears, and respiratory tract. They also develop enlarged lymph nodes, tonsils, and spleen.

The Sleep Health segment provides sleep therapy equipment, supplies and related services (including CPAP and BiLevel services) to individuals for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea. The Respiratory Health segment provides oxygen and home mechanical ventilation equipment and supplies and related chronic therapy services to individuals for the treatment of respiratory diseases, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and chronic respiratory failure. The Diabetes Health segment provides medical devices, including continuous glucose monitors and insulin pumps, and related services to patients for the treatment of diabetes. The Wellness at Home segment provides home medical equipment and services to patients in their homes including those who have been discharged from acute care and other facilities. The segment tailors a service model to patients who are adjusting to new lifestyles or navigating complex disease states by providing essential medical supplies and durable medical equipment.

The Company is proud to partner with an extensive and highly diversified network of referral sources, including acute care hospitals, sleep labs, pulmonologists, skilled nursing facilities, and clinics. data.title: Rent the Runway shares stumble as fewer subscribers, cash needs weigh
data.description:
Rent the Runway is limping into the end of the week at an all-time low and five straight days of losses as another decline in active subscribers and a fresh share offering outweighed constructive Q2 results and a new CEO.

Shares were down by nearly 20% at midday.

Thanks to a subscription price increase and an increase in the volume of add-on bookings, total revenue for the quarter increased 20.8%, and rental revenue was up 21% year-over-year.

This was overshadowed, however, by 3.8% fewer active subscribers in the second quarter, an outcome interim CFO David Loretta attributes to the stronger promotional activity last year and a higher rate of pause activity this year.

The company’s guidance also disappointed, as Q3 revenue guidance of $87M to $90M reflects flat to low single-digit growth compared to the same quarter last year. Full-year revenue growth was reaffirmed, and adjusted EBITDA margin is still expected to be between 4% and 7%.

Besides the loss in active subscribers and lackluster guidance, Rent the Runway shares were also pinned down by plans for a $15M rights offering and a $10M term loan, underscoring the company’s need for cash.
